provenance.derivation: Composed in the manner of kasane no irome, for autumn: 4 of our own published entries read as layers from the outermost inward — 雨岩 ame-iwa (#4F6678), then 刈跡 kari-ato (#B8996B), then 麻布 asa-nuno (#E5DFD4), then 秋夕 aki-yu (#722518). NOT a historical combination: no layer is asserted to reproduce a documented Heian kasane, and no value was read from any kasane table. Chosen by hand, not generated. Adjacent layers are separated by ΔE00 37.3, 21.6, 61.0 under @irodora/color-difference 0.1.0 — each above the ΔE00 5 at which the product calls two items the same (FR-44), because a layering whose edges cannot be told apart is not one. Weights fall inward (1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.5) because each inner layer shows less than the one over it.
provenance.editorialNotes: An autumn morning: a cool rain-grey (雨岩) outermost, the straw of a harvested field (刈跡), a pale linen layer (麻布) where the dew catches, and the dark red of autumn dusk (秋夕) as the innermost edge. The name is a seasonal image, not a documented kasane; it is the name mockup 10 draws for this row, adopted as ours because it describes these layers. The name is ours (秋の露, "Autumn Dew"), coined as a seasonal image the way the historical names are; it is not presented as a traditional kasane name.
